findings.title: Backup codes not invalidated after use on disable endpoint
findings.body: In disable.ts, when a backup code successfully matches, the code just proceeds (comment says 'we delete all stored backup codes at the end'). But the matched index is never nulled nor is a single-use check performed - this is fine because the whole backupCodes field is cleared when 2FA is disabled. However, if the TOTP/backup code check fails validation elsewhere (e.g., only disabling but code is reused across multiple requests before 2FA is actually disabled, e.g. concurrent requests), the same backup code could be reused multiple times before the user update commits, since there's no atomic consumption. This is a minor race but worth flagging as a correctness gap relative to the login flow in next-auth-options.ts which explicitly consumes (nulls) the backup code.

findings.title: Backup code lookup does not skip already-used (null) codes correctly and allows case/format mismatches
findings.body: backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '')) finds the first matching code, but used codes are set to null (line 148), so there's no issue with reuse of consumed codes. However, there's no normalization (e.g. lowercase) of user input before comparison, while codes are generated via crypto.randomBytes(...).toString('hex') which is lowercase hex. If a user copies/pastes with different casing (e.g., auto-caps on mobile), the backup code will incorrectly fail even though it is valid, causing legitimate lockout. This should normalize case before comparing.

findings.title: Exported component named TwoFactor instead of BackupCode
findings.body: The default export function is named `TwoFactor` even though the file is BackupCode.tsx and it's imported elsewhere as `BackupCode`. This is misleading/confusing for maintainers and could cause confusion when debugging (e.g., in React DevTools component names will show 'TwoFactor' for the backup code input).

findings.title: backupCodes state typed as never[] due to missing generic
findings.body: `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([]);` has no type annotation, so TypeScript infers `never[]`, which may cause type errors (or implicit any) when later calling `.map((code) => ...)` with `code` typed as `never`, and prevents compile-time safety for the backup codes array of strings returned by the API.

findings.title: resetForm clears password on reset after successful disable, but lostAccess toggle keeps password typed, risk of stale state
findings.body: resetForm(false) called from the 'lost access'/'go back' toggle does not clear password, which is fine, but after a successful disable, resetForm() (default clearPassword=true) clears password and codes, yet modal is not necessarily closed/unmounted before onDisable() runs; if the modal remains mounted and reopened, previous errorMessage state is cleared, but twoFactorLostAccess flag was already reset separately - this is a minor state management inconsistency without an actual bug but worth checking the modal fully resets between opens, as there's no reset tied to `open` prop toggling via useEffect.
